tagline: Out to the cape, then the back road to the cranberries.
intro: From North Bend the Cape Arago Highway runs out through Charleston, a working fishing port by the entrance to Coos Bay, and past a string of state parks to Cape Arago, where it ends 200 feet above the Pacific. Then it is six miles back to Seven Devils Road, which turns south past South Slough and Bandon's cranberry bogs to the Old Town.
Cranberries have grown around Bandon since 1885, when Charles McFarlin, who had come west for gold and failed to make a living at it, planted vines he brought from Cape Cod.
season: TripCheck gives spring through fall as the best time, and winter for whale watching.

moments.title: Sunset Bay State Park
moments.text: Sandstone cliffs ring the beach and warm the water enough for swimming, and stumps of a spruce forest drowned by an earthquake about 1,200 years ago lie along the shore.

moments.title: Shore Acres State Park
moments.text: Five acres of gardens from timber baron Louis Simpson's estate are open on the bluff, restored by the state, which bought the land from him in 1942.

moments.title: Bandon
moments.text: George Bennett named the town for his home in County Cork, and he also brought in gorse, which went wild and grows too thick for a person to walk through.
